links.cause: correctly rounded maths instead of glibc's

chain.note: Each box holds runs that give the same bytes. Here ANTs 2.6.5 gave 1 distinct result in 6 runs at 8 threads (at 12, 1 distinct result in 3); fMRIPrep's run at 8 threads, with its own ANTs 2.6.2 build, gave another, although at one thread the two builds give the same bytes: at several threads the result depends on how the threads share the image (ANTS-42). larmorx gives ANTs' one-thread result with correctly rounded maths on any number of threads; its default mode then corrects ANTS-43 (the metrics below).

examples.metrics_note: Δ is A − B. Every number is computed in float64 over all 5,898,240 voxels of the 160 × 192 × 192 outputs, not only the brain shown; the range is B's maximum minus its minimum. The rows *the original against itself* are ANTs' own variability on this input: its thread counts, two runs at 8 threads, its version.
